**Date:** {{< meta display-date >}}  
**From:** {{< meta from-address >}}  
**Manuscript Location:** {{< meta manuscript-location >}}  

My dear [Mrs Curteis](../persons.html#2034)
I send the gains of Mrs Twitch and of the bits of correspondence.[^1] St Canace’s Jackdaw is in type waiting till he can get in, and I think the Story of a Dream will probably be in before Alec as it is so much shorter and I think it is very good

Yours sincerely

C M Yonge

[^1]: Black-edged paper.

[^2]: \'Mrs.

Twitch\' was a story, signed R. L. C., published in MP (June 1869) 606-12, which gave rise to a query answered in (October 1869) 415.

Two later stories, also about Mrs Twitch and presumably by the same author, were \'Pin-Baskets\' (June 1875) 639-646, and \'True and Just in All My Dealings\' (September 1881) 300-3. \'St.

Canace\'s Jackdaw\' was a poem, published in MP (August 1869) 140-1.

The other stories mentioned have not been traced.
